formation.explanation: ApplyLog queues a future. Leader admission checks transfer and step-down, dispatch assigns index/term and stores locally before reporting self support. Ordinary follower append checks predecessor and stores before success; replication turns success into an index report. The voter-only accumulator takes a majority order statistic with a current-leader startIndex threshold. Leader consumption queues the committed prefix to the FSM; the single-entry FSM branch completes the future after Apply. Batching and user restore still require integration into this partial trace. Snapshot recovery now has a separate sourced support chain: receiver finalizes and restores before success; sender reports snapshot index. Vote receivers check identity/eligibility, leader knowledge, term, prior vote and last-log order, then persist before granting. Candidate majority grants enter leadership. AppendEntries and higher-term election responses can end authority. Ordinary follower append rejects old term or predecessor mismatch, truncates conflicting suffix and stores before success. Ordinary and pipeline replication report successful nonempty request boundaries to their captured commitment; snapshot transfer reports the finalized/restored snapshot boundary. Commitment keeps only latest voters, takes a majority order statistic, and advances only at or beyond the leader startIndex. Leader commit notification records commitment/configuration and queues the committed prefix to the FSM. Commands complete after single/batch application; barriers pass through the same worker; no-ops can finish without an FSM callback. context.explanation: Startup reads stable term/log tail, installs snapshot metadata and normally restores FSM, then scans later configuration entries before workers start. Bootstrap seeds clean state; forced RecoverCluster and Restore explicitly permit disaster-recovery replacement. Follower contact timeout and latest voter eligibility enter candidacy. Optional pre-vote tests proposed authority without persisting term, then real election persists term/self-vote and counts voter-targeted replies on campaign-local channels. Receivers enforce term, known-leader, candidate eligibility, prior-vote and history-order checks. Higher-term requests/replies, inadequate recent voter contact, negative verification or committed self-removal can cause authority loss. Transfer waits for target replication progress then TimeoutNow starts a normal majority election with transfer exceptions. Independent heartbeats refresh contact and verification separately from durable log support. F-elected-role records only the local quorum-tally transition; the main dispatcher subsequently consumes local Leader state to enter runLeader, subject to shutdown.

connection.explanation: Each leadership generation creates zeroed voter matches and startIndex=lastIndex+1, dispatches a no-op, and gives workers the generation commitment pointer and step-down channel. Exit stops workers and fails remaining inflight/verification futures; already committed FSM tuples survive on their serialized queue. Durable prior logs constrain new elections by term/index freshness, but need fresh generation support before commitment. Configuration changes require the prior configuration and a current-term entry committed; latest configuration immediately changes voter filtering, preserving matches by continuing ID. Snapshot creation binds an applied FSM boundary to a committed configuration before log compaction, while startup/installation restores those contexts. User Restore aborts remaining inflight work, serializes restoration after queued FSM work and burns a log index so subsequent replication uses the snapshot; its special recovery contract is distinct from normal preservation. The local role transition is the explicit connection from the election owner to fresh leader-generation initialization, not an assumed global leadership guarantee.

formation.explanation: ApplyLog queues a future. Leader admission checks transfer and step-down, dispatch assigns index/term and stores locally before reporting self support. Ordinary follower append checks predecessor and stores before success; replication turns success into an index report. The voter-only accumulator takes a majority order statistic with a current-leader startIndex threshold. Leader consumption queues the committed prefix to the FSM; the single-entry FSM branch completes the future after Apply. Batching and user restore still require integration into this partial trace. Snapshot recovery now has a separate sourced support chain: receiver finalizes and restores before success; sender reports snapshot index. Pipeline decoder registers nonempty successful request boundaries, but its future error contract remains open.

context.explanation: Candidate campaigns use election-local response channels, optional pre-vote and voter-targeted requests. Vote receivers check identity/eligibility, leader knowledge, term, prior vote and last-log order, then persist before granting. Candidate majority grants enter leadership. AppendEntries and higher-term election responses can end authority. New leadership allocates fresh aggregation and workers; exit stops workers, fails pending inflight operations and clears leader state. Follower timeout, persistence helpers, pre-vote, lease and transfer need full tracing.

connection.explanation: Durable log history can survive leadership loss, but the new commitment object starts with zero matches and requires an entry at or beyond its new startIndex. Workers capture the object and step-down channel for their generation. Configuration filtering changes which IDs count while retaining matches for continuing voters. Election log-order checks connect stored history to authority acquisition. Committed futures removed from inflight may still await the separate FSM worker; clearing leader state is not equivalent to cancelling all application. Startup recovers current term and log tail, restores snapshot boundary/configuration, then scans later configuration entries before launching workers. Runtime snapshot install also replaces the local latest and committed configuration after restoration.

formation.explanation: ApplyLog queues a future; a leader rejects transfer/step-down admission, assigns index and term, stores the batch, then reports its own match.
